children: Less than a month after Warren Buffett stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway's chairman, the company's Class B stock is on a tear.
Berkshire's Class B stock was trading above $521 a share, up 0.7% on Tuesday and on pace for its highest close since Sept. 16, when it closed at $519.80 and Buffett was still chairman.

The stock is currently up nine consecutive days, and on its longest winning streak in more than two years. It last rose for nine straight days ending Sept. 4, 2024, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
The stock is up 3.8% year to date and up 5.2% over the past 12 months.

Buffett retired as CEO of Berkshire at the end of 2025 and was succeeded by current CEO Greg Abel. He stepped down as chair on Sept. 18, and was succeeded in that role by his son, Howard, a Berkshire director since 1993.
Warren Buffett remains chairman emeritus of the company and is on the board.
